clue.text: Product I slipped into beautiful girls' drinks

indicators.note: something slipped into a container is put inside it, so these pieces go within the girls' word

parts.note: peaches is old slang for attractive young women
a brand is a named product on sale

explanation.surface: A sinister picture of someone spiking young women's drinks at a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a spiked drink, but 'slipped into' is a container signal and 'beautiful girls' is old slang, not the drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Peach brandy is a fruit-flavoured spirit, so the plural names a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Planned to sort out means of producing erection

indicators.note: sort out means to put in order, so the words beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a scheme to provide a remedy for impotence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erection' suggests something smutty; it is a building, put up using a Dorset limestone.
explanation.definitionFit: This pale limestone from Dorset is a building material used for many grand edifices, such as St Paul's Cathedral.

clue.text: Demonstration after head's ousted principal

indicators.note: the first letter of the demonstration word is thrown out

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

explanation.surface: Protests follow the removal of a school principal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal' looks like a school head; it is the adjective meaning chief, as in arch-enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means chief or leading, as in an arch rival.

clue.text: Ring Chistopher Robin's friend up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is the bear who befriends Christopher Robin in A A Milne's stories

explanation.surface: An order to phone Christopher Robin's friend, Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue misspells Christopher as printed. 'Ring' looks like a phone call; it is the noun meaning a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band, a ring of wood or metal.

clue.text: See 1
Delta? A character that speaks volumes

definitions.meaning: the delta of a river is where it widens into a huge opening onto the sea
someone who talks too much and boastfully

explanation.surface: Delta? A character that speaks volumes
explanation.definitionFit: A delta is a river's wide outlet, while a boastful chatterer is a loudmouth.

clue.text: White Britain's going backwards

indicators.note: one letter of the old name for Britain steps back to the end of the word

parts.note: Albion is an old poetic name for Britain

explanation.surface: A lament that Britain is in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going backwards' moves the O back one place, so ALBION becomes ALBINO.
explanation.definitionFit: An albino lacks pigment, so has very pale skin and hair.

clue.text: See 1
International champion and German taking all things into consideration

parts.note: a champion of a cause is its hero
und is the German word for and

explanation.surface: A world-class winner and a German compatriot weighing everything up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and German' is one piece: 'and' in German is UND.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen in the round means considered from every side, fully and comprehensively.

clue.text: Ordered to take off immediately with bombs and set course?

parts.note: fighter pilots are scrambled when ordered to get airborne at once
eggs is RAF slang for bombs

explanation.surface: Fighter pilots ordered up urgently with bombs to lay a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set course' is a fixed menu course, as at a breakfast or brunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of beaten cooked eggs often served as part of a set breakfast menu.

clue.text: Prominence of disputed territory indicates Blair got far

parts.note: read as instructions, the answer says rock (shake up) the letters of its last two words, and they spell out this phrase

explanation.surface: A political commentator claims a famous landmark shows how far Tony Blair rose.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer itself is the wordplay, with 'rock' as the signal to shake up OF GIBRALTAR, producing BLAIRGOTFAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The great limestone promontory dominates Gibraltar, a British territory whose sovereignty Spain contests.

clue.text: Weight is borne by wood floor

indicators.note: carried inside, so the weight and is go within the wood

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A wooden floor carries a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor' looks like a noun; it is the verb meaning to stun.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to amaze or stagger them.

clue.text: Bluewater is nearer the Thames estuary than London?

definitions.text: Bluewater is nearer the Thames estuary than London?

parts.words: Bluewater is nearer the Thames estuary than London?
parts.note: Bluewater, a big Kent shopping centre, lies further along the river towards the sea than London; split, blue gives down (sad) and water gives stream

explanation.surface: A geography quiz question about where a shopping centre sits relative to the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Bluewater is a large shopping centre in Kent, east of London towards the Thames estuary. Cryptically blue = DOWN and water = STREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Places towards a river's mouth lie further along its current, in the direction the water flows.

clue.text: See 1
In favour of region employing university's legal representative

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of

indicators.note: the region uses the university, taking it inside itself

parts.note: a sector is an area or region
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Support for a district that hires a university's lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosecutor is the lawyer who brings a criminal case for the state.

clue.text: Display area for Tiffany's frozen spit?

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds, the stock of Tiffany, the New York jeweller
a shelf is where goods are set out for show

explanation.surface: A jeweller's window display, then a puzzle about frozen saliva.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spit' suggests saliva; it is a narrow point of land jutting into the sea, here made of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating sheet of glacial ice jutting from a coast is like a frozen projecting spit of land.

clue.text: Outrage customer fleeced by substantial settlement

indicators.note: a fleeced sheep has lost its outer coat, so the customer word loses its outside letters

parts.note: a patron is a regular customer of a shop or restaurant
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A shopper overcharged by a big town complains of an outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleeced' looks like 'cheated' but means stripped of its outer letters, like a shorn sheep; 'by' means beside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a shocking, wicked act that provokes public indignation.

clue.text: Bury's within Patient Ombudsman's remit

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, across the word break

explanation.surface: Bury, the Lancashire town, falls under the Patient Ombudsman's remit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' reads as the Lancashire town, but is the verb to inter; the letters are inside patiENT OMBudsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a corpse in a tomb is to inter or lay it to rest.

clue.text: See 8
Shows written about leading characters in Ray Bradbury book

indicators.note: the shows word goes round the leading letters

parts.note: to prove is to show to be true

indicators.note: the first letters of the author's two names

explanation.surface: Shows adapted from a Ray Bradbury novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' looks like a Bradbury novel but is the Book of Proverbs in the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbs is a book of the Old Testament, a collection of wise sayings.

clue.text: Refrain from Jerusalem essentially penned by non-atheist

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed within it, as in a pen

parts.note: a deist believes in a god, so is not an atheist

indicators.note: the essence or heart of the city's name, its central letter

explanation.surface: A believer is asked to stay away from Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a noun (a chorus) but is the verb; S, the middle of the nine-letter Jerusalem, goes inside DEIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to hold back or stop doing something, a close synonym of ceasing.

clue.text: Religious education New College dons understand after priest's attendance

indicators.note: placed after the priest, so that piece comes first in the word

parts.note: P is a standard abbreviation for priest
RE is the school subject's abbreviation

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so these letters wear the understand word around them

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in I see

explanation.surface: Oxford dons at New College grasp RE lessons, after a priest's visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like Oxford lecturers at New College but means puts on: N and C are clothed by SEE, making SENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present at an event is the same as attending it.

clue.text: Resolve a maths problem with laboured breathing

indicators.note: to resolve is to break down and recompose, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student struggles to solve a maths problem, gasping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' seems to go with maths but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a respiratory condition causing wheezing and difficulty getting air.

clue.text: Writer's getting hit first in a row

indicators.note: tells us the hit piece is put at the front, ahead of the writer's

parts.note: a hit is a success, like a chart-topping song
the writer is I, the setter, and writer's here is I have, contracted to I've

explanation.surface: An author's latest book is a smash, coming top of the list.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter refers to themself as 'writer', so 'Writer's' = I'VE, with SUCCESS put first.
explanation.definitionFit: Things in a row follow one after another, consecutively.

clue.text: See 1
Crop head of state out of good shot

indicators.note: the monarch's letters are taken out of the marksman

parts.note: a sniper is a skilled marksman
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the British head of state

explanation.surface: An order to cut a president out of a nice photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a photo; it is a marksman. ER (the Queen) is removed from SNIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: To crop and to snip both mean to cut short.

clue.text: Unfamiliarity's helping creator of fiction

indicators.note: a helping is a portion of something, so only part of the word is served

explanation.surface: Not knowing a subject helps a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in unfamiLIARity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tells untruths makes up stories, a teller of fiction.

clue.text: See 8
Wanting article on being unlikely to win

parts.note: to be out of something is to be lacking or wanting it
the is the definite article
a machine that is on is running

explanation.surface: A newspaper is short of a piece about someone who is a long shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is not a link: it means working, as an engine that is on is RUNNING.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor with no realistic chance is said to have dropped out of contention.

clue.text: Somehow stop our press covering article in international papers

indicators.note: the rearranged letters lie over and around the article
suggests the letters come together in some unspecified way, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor urges that a story be stopped from going to print, somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' shuffles STOP OUR PRESS into EUROPSSPORTS, which is 'covering' A, giving EUROPASSPORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are travel documents issued in a common format across the European Union's member states.
